title: Signal Playbook: Personal KPIs and Weekly Check-ins
content:
Quick intent: a light-weight, signal-first personal KPI system for Q1–Q2 2026. Not an OKR manifesto — just a practical scratchpad for what I actually measure week-to-week and why.

Why this exists
- I get distracted by long lists and vanity metrics. Need a simple filter: keep metrics where I can see cause->effect in 1–3 sprints.
- Goal: surface 2 outcome metrics (north-star-ish) + 3 leading indicators + 3 micro-experiments at any time.

North-star / Outcome metrics (quarter focus)
- Product adoption: new active feature users (weekly MAU subset for feature X). Target: +12% quarter-over-quarter. (Signal: featureX_weekly_active)
- Latency impact on funnel: % requests meeting latency budget and conversion delta. Target: keep conversion loss < 1.0% when latency > baseline. (Signal: latency_tail_pct, funnel_conversion_by_latency_bucket)

Why these two?
- Adoption maps to actual value created.
- Latency is both an engineering lever and a product experience issue that shows up quickly in funnel numbers.

Leading indicators (track weekly)
- Experiment velocity: number of experiment iterations merged + deployed (goal: 2/wk).
- Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of alerts: % actionable vs noisy (goal: increase actionable share to 45%).
- Demo conversions: number of demo signups who enable feature X in first 2 weeks (goal: +8%).

Micro-experiments (current batch) — short lived, hypothesis + guardrail
1) Default prompt tweak for onboarding wizard
   - Hypothesis: changing default prompt improves completion -> more users try advanced flow.
   - Metric: % who click "Try advanced" within 7 days. Target +6pp.
   - Risk: confusion -> monitor dropoff in onboarding; rollback immediately if drop > 5pp.
   - Status: A/B started 2026-03-02, see JIRA-OPS-842.

2) Small latency budget rollback for heavy routes (canary)
   - Hypothesis: enforcing tighter tail reduces token cost and keeps core users engaged.
   - Metric: cost-per-request delta + 7-day retention for affected cohort.
   - Status: staging tests green; scheduling canary next week.

3) Quick docs prompt card in console
   - Hypothesis: short how-to increases "success on first try" for new teams.
   - Metric: success_on_first_try rate (internal metric).
   - Status: design prototype, needs copy review.

Weekly check-in template (5–10 minutes)
- Top-line numbers (2 outcomes): new feature users this week; latency_budget_met_pct (weekly).
- Leading indicators: experiment velocity, SNR %, demo conversion.
- Quick notes: 3 wins, 3 blockers.
- Next actions: 3 tiny commitments for the coming week.
- Confidence check: how confident am I that actions move the outcomes? (low/med/high)

This week's snapshot (2026-03-11)
- Outcome: featureX_weekly_active = +2.4% w/w (trending toward Q-target but slow).
- Latency: tail 95th increased 8% last 2 days after deploy (investigate).
- Leading indicators: Experiment velocity = 1 merged (below target). SNR actionable = 32% (need cleanup). Demo conversions flat.
- Wins: shipped onboarding tweak A; cleaned two noisy alerts; clarified docs flow in console prototype.
- Blockers: infra canary blocked by capacity reservations; copy review delayed; unclear metric mapping for success_on_first_try.
- Confidence: medium (some levers require infra help).

Immediate actions (this sprint)
- Add a small canary capacity request to infra queue (owner: Lina Chen) — ticket created.
- Add tracing to new deploy to measure 95th tail by route (owner: self; estimate 2h).
- Schedule quick copy sync with Product writer (30m).

Measurement notes / experiment hygiene
- Always include: hypothesis, primary metric, guardrail, minimum detectable effect (MDE) estimate, rollout plan, rollback trigger.
- Small experiments: aim for short duration (3–10 days) and clear stop criteria.
- Avoid splitting the analysis across more than two primary metrics; pick one canonical metric + secondary guardrail.

Mental model: signal-first pruning
- Every week, prune 1 metric that feels too noisy or disconnected from an action I can take this week.
- If an experiment runs > 3 weeks without clear signal, archive and summarize lessons.

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- Consider measuring time-to-first-success (TTFS) as a complementary metric to adoption; often high-correlation with long-term retention.
- Think about a simple dashboard that shows only the two outcomes + one leading indicator card (mobile-style). Less noise equals faster decisions.
- Could frame the latency work as a product quality OKR in Q2 with product ops sponsoring.

Unresolved questions
- How to best attribute demo conversions to featureX exposure vs sales outreach? (talk to growth analytics)
- Can I automate the SNR calculation from current alerting tooling? If so, what's the cheapest way to approximate it?

Archive / threads to export
- Capture quick retrospective notes after any experiment ends: one paragraph summary, top metric delta, lesson learned. Put in confluence: confluence:personal-goals-2026/experiments.

Quick TODO (today)
- 1. Add tracing instrumentation (2h)
- 2. Ping Product writer for copy (slack)
- 3. Triage noisy alerts list and label top 5 candidates for mute

End — keep this short and actionable. Revisit weekly on Wed morning during quiet hour.

----
Meta: draft personal playbook, intentionally informal. Will refine into a 1-page quarter plan if I can maintain the weekly cadence for 4 weeks.
